rows.judge_notes: The strongest layer is the rules and the server: game/rules.js is pure and deterministic, and the server checks every intent against availableActions() and rate-limits it. A scripted solo run took the wolf quest from accept to turn-in and level 2, 50 buy/sell loops lost gold (30 to 3), injected action names and repeat turn-ins were rejected, and all 11 tests pass under node --test. The weakest layer is operations and brand: only PORT and SAVE_FILE come from the environment, with no stated difference between development and production; there are no feature flags; privacy covers obligations but never lists what personal data is stored or where; there is no stated brand voice; and the only social post is one Tweet/Bluesky text with emoji (the Steam blurb is a store description, not a social post). Yes, I would fund M1: the docs make specific, well-argued decisions (zone shards, a Postgres ledger, no loot boxes, Tolkien IP avoidance), are honest about what is prototype-only, and the 9–12 month plan for a team of four is credible.
